text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- U.S. aircraft carrier Enterprise starts policing southern Iraq no-fly zone.

- Parliament approves Kuwait Municipality budget. MPs had withheld approval of the municipality budget for a few weeks because of its dismantling of private farms built on state-owned land by Kuwaitis.
- Iran to allow Kuwaitis to buy residential property, ambassador says.
- Russia renews its full support for Kuwait's sovereignty.
- Kuwait Airways Corp ranks fourth in terms of passenger traffic in the Middle East, IATA says.

- Kuwaiti Islamic Affairs Minister to visit Jordan to take part in the Islamic Conference Organisation meeting. The visit is the first by a Kuwaiti cabinet minister to Amman since the 1990-91 Gulf crisis when ties between the two Arab states were badly strained over Jordan's sympathy with Kuwait's former occupier Iraq.
- Employment contracts of 200 health ministry workers terminated. Kuwait is trying to reduce dependence on non-Kuwaiti workers.
